questions.questionText: When did apartheid officially begin?
questions.explanation: The National Party won the 1948 election and began implementing apartheid policies immediately.

questions.questionText: What was the Population Registration Act?

options.text: Classified all South Africans by race

questions.explanation: The Act required all South Africans to be classified as White, Black, or Coloured, determining their legal rights.

questions.questionText: What were the Group Areas Act's purpose?

options.text: Forced segregation of residential areas by race

questions.explanation: Group Areas Act forcibly removed communities and designated separate areas for different race groups.

questions.questionText: Who was Hendrik Verwoerd?

options.text: Prime Minister known as 'Architect of Apartheid'

questions.explanation: Verwoerd was Prime Minister from 1958-1966 and shaped apartheid into comprehensive legal system.

questions.questionText: What were pass laws?

options.text: Documents required for black movement and labor

questions.explanation: Pass laws restricted black South Africans' movement, requiring permits to travel outside designated areas.

questions.questionText: What was the homeland (Bantustan) policy?
questions.explanation: Homelands policy relocated Africans to theoretically self-governing territories, denying citizenship in South Africa proper.

questions.questionText: What was the Suppression of Communism Act?
questions.explanation: The Act defined communism so broadly that virtually any anti-apartheid activity could be banned.

questions.questionText: How did apartheid affect education?
questions.explanation: Bantu Education Act created vastly inferior separate schools with instruction in African languages instead of English.

questions.questionText: What was the purpose of the Mixed Marriages Act?

options.text: Banned marriages between different race groups

questions.explanation: Mixed Marriages Act prohibited marriage between white and non-white persons to maintain racial purity.

questions.questionText: How did apartheid control labor?

options.text: Through influx control and migrant labor systems

questions.explanation: Influx control laws restricted African urbanization while keeping mines and industries supplied with cheap labor.

questions.questionText: What was Sharpeville and what happened there?

options.text: 1960 massacre where police killed 69 peaceful protesters

questions.explanation: Sharpeville massacre on March 21, 1960 marked turning point when police fired on anti-pass law protesters.

questions.questionText: What was the Immorality Act?
questions.explanation: Immorality Act criminalized extramarital sexual relations between white and non-white persons.

questions.questionText: How did apartheid affect sporting opportunities?

options.text: Mandated separate competitions with unequal resources

questions.explanation: Separate sports bodies controlled access, funding, and facilities, limiting opportunities for black athletes.

questions.questionText: What was the Natives Abolition of Passes Act?

options.text: Combined pass laws into one system of control

questions.explanation: The Act consolidated existing pass laws, requiring Africans to carry reference books at all times.

questions.questionText: Analyze the ideological foundations of apartheid.

options.text: Based on pseudo-scientific racism and Afrikaner nationalism

questions.explanation: Apartheid drew from religious interpretations, scientific racism, and fears of racial mixing.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the impact of apartheid on South Africa's economy.

options.text: Created cheap labor system benefiting white workers at expense of majority

questions.explanation: Apartheid created structural advantages for whites through controlled labor, land dispossession, and unequal development.

questions.questionText: To what extent did international pressure affect apartheid?

options.text: Created isolation but also strengthened government's 'besieged' mentality

questions.explanation: International condemnation and sanctions isolated South Africa while reinforcing government's claims of white survival.

questions.questionText: Analyze how apartheid controlled daily life beyond laws.

options.text: Through comprehensive bureaucratic control of movement, residence, and employment

questions.explanation: Apartheid extended beyond laws into daily life through permits, pass offices, and bureaucratic categorization.

questions.questionText: How did Verwoerd develop apartheid beyond previous segregation?

options.text: Theorized separate development rather than just separation

questions.explanation: Verwoerd argued for 'separate development' giving ethnic groups their own homelands, not just segregation.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the legacy of apartheid legislation on post-apartheid South Africa.

options.text: Created lasting spatial, economic, and social inequalities

questions.explanation: Despite legal abolition, apartheid's spatial, economic, and educational legacies continue to shape South African society.
